passage: Afreen began taking the longer lane past the flour mill so she would not pass Jagdish at the tea stall. She told her cousins she did not care. But every day she slowed down at the spot where they used to share roasted peanuts, and on the local bus her hand kept going to the empty seat beside her. One evening she sat on the terrace and said quietly to the darkening sky, "I miss him. I miss how we were." Saying it made her chest hurt a little less. The next day she told her aunt, "I lost my best friend," and her aunt sat down beside her and made tea. Afreen did not call Jagdish. But she stopped pretending.

qa.q: Which way did Afreen take after the betrayal?
qa.a: She took the longer lane past the flour mill.

qa.q: What was Afreen feeling when she slowed down at the peanut spot, though she told her cousins she did not care?
qa.a: She was grieving the friendship; she pretended not to care, but slowing down and reaching for the empty seat show how much she missed him.

qa.q: How did naming her loss help Afreen?
qa.a: Saying it aloud made her chest hurt less and let her aunt sit with her, so she did not carry it alone.

qa.q: How might Afreen's aunt see her that day?
qa.a: As someone who was hurting and needed company more than advice, since she sat down beside Afreen and made tea.

grounding: A teen mourns the loss of a friendship after a betrayal; naming the grief helps instead of pretending not to care.

passage: Three weeks after Xin told the whole robotics club that Emil had cried at his grandfather's funeral, Emil still walked the long way round their Vancouver school so he wouldn't pass her locker. At lunch he said, "Honestly, I don't even care any more," and laughed too loudly. That night he found their old shared playlist and couldn't stop scrolling: songs from bus rides, the silly one they sang at the science fair. His chest ached. At breakfast his mother noticed his untouched toast. Emil stared at the table. "I miss her. Not what she did. Her. It's like someone died, but she's still in my maths class." His mother sat down beside him. "That's grief. It makes sense." Saying it out loud didn't fix anything, but his shoulders came down.

qa.q: What did Xin tell the robotics club?
qa.a: Xin told them that Emil had cried at his grandfather's funeral.

qa.q: What was Emil feeling as he scrolled through the old playlist?
qa.a: Emil felt grief and loss for the friendship, an ache in his chest that his "I don't care" laugh had hidden.

qa.q: Why did saying "I miss her" help more than "I don't care"?
qa.a: Naming the grief out loud let his mother recognise it and comfort him, while pretending not to care kept the ache hidden.

qa.q: How might Xin experience Emil walking the long way round her locker?
qa.a: Xin may feel guilty and shut out, sensing she has lost her best friend.

grounding: Illustrates a teen mourning a friendship lost to a betrayed secret, and how naming the grief helps more than pretending not to care.

passage: In the girls' hostel in Dehradun, Rukmini moved her bed to the far end of the dorm after Rekha read her poem notebook aloud to the others. They had shared a study table for three years. Now they passed in the mess without a word. Rukmini told everyone she was fine, busier and happier than ever. But on Sunday evening she sat on the steps behind the laundry and cried until her nose ran. The warden, Mrs Negi, found her there and sat on the step below. "You've lost your closest friend. That's a real loss, even if she's still here." Rukmini nodded. "I keep turning round to tell her things." "Then let yourself be sad about it for a while," Mrs Negi said. "Pretending costs more."

qa.q: How long had Rukmini and Rekha shared a study table?
qa.a: They had shared a study table for three years.

qa.q: What was Rukmini feeling on the steps behind the laundry?
qa.a: Rukmini felt deep sadness and grief for the lost friendship, which she had been hiding by acting fine.

qa.q: How did Mrs Negi help Rukmini?
qa.a: Mrs Negi named the loss as real and gave Rukmini permission to be sad instead of pretending.

qa.q: How might Rekha see Rukmini moving her bed to the far end?
qa.a: Rekha may feel the distance as a sharp punishment, and perhaps regret, realising how much she broke.

grounding: Shows a teen grieving a best friendship broken by a betrayed secret, and an adult helping her name the grief instead of pretending.
